## Desktop

### Improvements
- OpenCode 1 now offers the upgrade to OpenCode 2.0. OpenCode 2 downloads in the background and installs only when you choose: Restart to upgrade, Upgrade on quit, or Later. Your sessions, projects, and settings are kept. Plugins made for OpenCode 1 need an update.

## Core

### Bugfixes
- Sessions with many images no longer send oversized requests. When the images in a session's history pass 25 MiB, the oldest are replaced with a placeholder.
- A provider error for a request body that is too large now starts compaction and a retry instead of failing the turn.

title: "Console models"
description: "Curated coding models, pay-as-you-go pricing, and API access through OpenCode Console."
---

OpenCode Console provides a list of models tested and verified by the OpenCode team. Sign in, add credits, and get an
API key to use them with OpenCode or another coding agent.

Console works like any other provider in OpenCode. It's **completely optional**, and you can use any other provider
instead. For a subscription with included usage, see [OpenCode Go](/console/go).

## How it works

1. Sign in to the [console](https://opencode.ai/console), add your billing details and credits, and copy your API key.
2. Run `/connect` in the TUI, choose the OpenCode pay-as-you-go provider, and paste your API key.

   ```text
   /connect
   ```

3. Run `/models` to see the available models and select one.

   ```text
   /models
   ```

You are charged per request and can add credits to your account.

## Endpoints

You can also access the models directly through the following API endpoints. Free-tier chat models require OpenCode;
use paid models or [Go](/console/go) from other clients.

Each model is listed with its native API, but every text model also works through the other APIs, which Console
translates. See [Base URLs](/console/harnesses#base-urls) for the full set.

### Jev

Jev is a System One model from TypeSafe AI for fast, structured decisions. Instead of generating text, it evaluates a `state` against typed questions and returns values and probabilities that your code can use directly. It supports yes/no (`noul`), multiple-choice (`choice`), and rubric-based (`score`) questions.

Use your OpenCode Console API key with the `https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone` endpoint. This example checks whether a support request is urgent:

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-1.14",
    "state": "My payments have failed for three days and I am losing sales. Please help now.",
    "questions": {
      "is_urgent": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Does this request require urgent attention?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

You can ask multiple questions in one request. Jev evaluates them in parallel and returns each answer under the matching question ID:

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "jev-1.14",
    "state": "My order arrived late and the item is damaged. I want a refund.",
    "questions": {
      "department": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Which team should handle this request?",
        "criteria": {
          "returns": "Refunds, exchanges, or damaged items",
          "shipping": "Delivery delays or lost packages",
          "billing": "Charges, invoices, or payment problems"
        }
      },
      "frustration": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How frustrated is the customer?",
        "criteria": ["Calm", "Frustrated", "Very angry"]
      }
    }
  }'
```

Use `jev-1.13-free` to use the limited-time free model, which runs Jev 1.13. See the [TypeSafe AI documentation](https://docs.typesafe.ai/) for details about question types and response fields.

### GPT 6 Luna Decision and Gemini Decision 1

`gpt-6-luna-decision` and `gemini-decision-1` take the same System One request as Jev, on the same endpoint. Pass images, audio, video, and PDFs in `state` as chat-style parts (`image_url`, `input_audio`, `video_url`, `file`). GPT 6 Luna Decision accepts text and images; Gemini Decision 1 also accepts audio, video, and PDFs.

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/systemone/v1/systemone \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gemini-decision-1",
    "state": "I was charged twice for my order.",
    "questions": {
      "refund": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is this a refund request?"
      }
    }
  }'
```

### Image models

`gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`, `gemini-nano-banana-2.1`, and `grok-imagine-image-2.0` generate and edit images. They aren't chat models, so they never appear in `/models` or the models endpoint,
and `opencode/<model-id>` doesn't select them. Call them on their native API with a Console key, or let OpenCode's
[`generate_image`](/tools#image-generate) tool use an image model by setting
`experimental.image_generate.model`, for example `opencode/gpt-image-2.5-sunburst`.

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/images/generations \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-image-2.5-sunburst",
    "prompt": "A mountain at sunrise",
    "size": "1024x1024"
  }'
```

Google takes its native `contents` and `generationConfig`, and xAI its native options such as `resolution` and
`quality`. OpenAI Images and xAI Images also accept edits at `/images/edits`.

### Embedding models

`text-embedding-3-small`, `qwen3-embedding-8b`, and the other embedding models in the table above turn text into
vectors. OpenCode doesn't use them for chat, so they never appear in `/models`, and the free tier doesn't include them.
[Go](/console/go#embedding-models) includes some of them. Call them on OpenAI's Embeddings API with a Console key.

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/openai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCODE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "text-embedding-3-small",
    "input": ["hello world", "goodbye"]
  }'
```

- `input` takes a string or an array of strings. `data` returns one vector per input, in the same order.
- `dimensions` shortens the vectors on models that support it, such as `text-embedding-3-small`.
- `encoding_format: "base64"` returns the vectors base64-encoded instead of as floats.
- Each input must fit in the model's context window.
- The response reports `usage.cost` like any inference request. See [Cost](/console/api/inference#cost).

Vectors from different models aren't comparable, so embed your documents and your queries with the same model. A

## Background

There are many models available, but only a few work well as coding agents. Providers also vary in configuration,
performance, and quality, so a model accessed through a gateway such as OpenRouter may perform differently.

<Callout type="tip">We tested a select group of models and providers that work well with OpenCode.</Callout>

To build this catalog, we:

1. Tested a select group of models and talked to their teams about how to best run them.
2. Worked with providers to make sure the models were served correctly.
3. Benchmarked each model/provider combination to produce a list we feel good recommending.

Console is an AI gateway that gives you access to these models.

## Goals

We built Console to:

1. **Benchmark** the best models and providers for coding agents.
2. Provide the **highest quality** options without downgrading performance or routing to cheaper providers.
3. Pass along **price drops** by selling at cost, with markup only to cover processing fees.
4. Have **no lock-in**: use Console with any coding agent, or use another provider with OpenCode.

## Where can I use it?

OpenCode Go is designed for [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and other coding agents
that produce similar types of requests. Traffic is monitored for abuse that
degrades the experience for other users.

Your client should:

1. Send typical coding agent traffic
2. Identify itself with its own user agent, such as `my-coding-agent/1.0`, rather
   than a generic SDK or HTTP-library name.
3. Send a stable session ID in `x-opencode-session` for each conversation so we can optimize routing and
   prompt caching.

[Decision](#decision-models) and [embedding](#embedding-models) requests don't need `x-opencode-session`, so any
client, such as a RAG library, a memory provider or a script, can call them with your Go key.

See [Harnesses](/console/harnesses) to set up Go in Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, Pi, and Raycast.

## Usage limits

The paid models you use on Go share one allowance. On Go Teams, each member has their own allowance across models.

- The **5-hour limit** is 20% of your monthly allowance. The window starts when you first use your allowance and lasts five hours.
- The **weekly limit** is 50% of your monthly allowance. It resets on Monday at 00:00 UTC.
- Your **monthly allowance** resets when a new paid period starts.

Switching models draws from the same allowance. If you reach a limit, you can use a free model or turn on
[Extra Usage](#usage-beyond-limits) to use your Console credits until you have allowance available again.

Each model's [monthly limit](https://opencode.ai/console/go#limits) shows how much usage your plan covers if you use only that model over the month.
For example, $1.50 of usage on a model with a $15 limit uses 10% of your monthly allowance. So does $6 on a model
with a $60 limit. Go responses report how much each request counted in [`opencode.allowance`](/console/api/inference#cost).

[Token prices](https://opencode.ai/console/go#pricing) are per 1M tokens and are the same for Go, Go Plus, and Go Teams.

[Decision](#decision-models) and [embedding](#embedding-models) models come at list price, with no Go discount: their
monthly limit matches what you pay, $10 on Go and $40 on Go Plus. On Go Teams it's $15, $5 higher than Go as on every
model.

**Beam Free:** Free for a limited time. Not available in Angola, Belarus, Cambodia, China (including Hong Kong and Macau), Cuba, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Iran, Iraq, Laos, Libya, Nigeria, North Korea, Russia, Syria, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Venezuela, or the Crimea, Donetsk, and Luhansk regions of Ukraine.

### Why some models have lower usage

With Go, the included monthly usage varies by model.

For most models, we make this work through bulk discounts and reserved GPU capacity. We then pass those savings on to you as higher monthly usage.

For some models, we haven't had the opportunity to negotiate a discount or host them at a lower cost, either because the model is new or because their public pricing is already discounted.

For these models, you still get a little more than if you paid the model providers directly; this is why their included monthly usage is lower.

### Usage

Check how much of your [usage limits](#usage-limits) you've used, for example to show them in your own client:

```bash
curl https://opencode.ai/inference/go/v1/usage \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

Use the same key you use for Go. On Go and Go Plus, that is the subscriber's
[personal API key](/console/api#personal-api-keys) or a [service account key](/console/api#service-accounts). On Go
Teams, it is any member's personal API key.

The response has one meter for each limit: `rolling` for the 5-hour limit, `weekly`, and `monthly`.

```json
{
  "usage": {
    "rolling": { "status": "ok", "percent": 30, "resetsAt": "2026-11-21T15:00:00.000Z" },
    "weekly": { "status": "rate-limited", "percent": 100, "resetsAt": "2026-11-23T00:00:00.000Z" },
    "monthly": { "status": "ok", "percent": 50, "resetsAt": "2026-12-01T00:00:00.000Z" }
  }
}
```

| Field      | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`   | `ok`, or `rate-limited` once the limit is used up.                                                         |
| `percent`  | How much of the limit is used, as a whole number from `0` to `100`.                                        |
| `resetsAt` | When the limit resets, in ISO 8601. Before the 5-hour window starts, `rolling` resets five hours from now. |

Requests without a valid key return HTTP `401`. Keys Go doesn't cover return HTTP `403` with a message that explains
why, for example when the workspace has no active Go subscription.

```json
{ "type": "error", "error": { "type": "EntitlementError", "message": "OpenCode Go subscription required." } }
```

## Background

Open models have gotten really good. They now reach performance close to proprietary models for coding tasks. Because many providers can serve them competitively, they are usually far cheaper.

However, getting reliable, low latency access to them can be difficult. Providers vary in quality and availability.

<Callout type="tip">We tested a select group of models and providers that work well with OpenCode.</Callout>

To fix this, we did a couple of things:

1. We tested a select group of open models and talked to their teams about how to best run them.
2. We worked with a few providers to make sure these were being served correctly.
3. We benchmarked the combination of the model/provider and came up with a list that we feel good recommending.

Go, Go Plus, and Go Teams all provide access to these models; choose the plan that fits how much you use them, or Go
Teams to cover your whole team.

## Goals

We created OpenCode Go to:

1. Make AI coding **accessible** to more people with a low cost subscription.
2. Provide **reliable** access to the best open coding models.
3. Curate models that are **tested and benchmarked** for coding agent use.
4. Have **no lock-in** by allowing you to use any other provider with OpenCode as well.
